_comment: Tier-2 for skfem navier_stokes#2, verified 2026-08-06 on skfem 12.0.1. Claim (already corrected once): the convection term needs ElementVector, no AttributeError announces it because CellBasis DOES have split, the no-argument call raises TypeError 'AbstractBasis.split() missing 1 required positional argument: x', and the working guard is a SHAPE check. Ran: MeshTri().refined(2), scalar ElementTriP2 (81 DOFs) vs ElementVector(ElementTriP2) (162), the split attribute and both call forms, convection assembled on each basis, and the wrong-sized block stacked with scipy.sparse.bmat. Printed: every part of the corrected entry reproduces -- class is CellBasis, split exists, the no-arg call raises the quoted TypeError verbatim, and split(x) returns one (array, basis) pair per dimension with scalar-sized arrays. The shape guard works: vector N is exactly dim times scalar N. The failure is silent and dimensional: the scalar convection block assembles to a perfectly valid square 81x81 matrix with non-zeros, exactly dim times too small for the 162x162 viscous block, and the only objection comes from scipy.sparse.bmat with ValueError 'inconsistent shapes' -- a message naming neither the basis nor the element.
